product.name: 18 V cordless drill/driver (generic, brushed)
product.pitch: A clamshell tool that turns battery energy into controlled torque at the chuck: motor, two-speed planetary gearbox, slip clutch, keyless chuck, trigger speed control.
evidence: Illustrative worked example assembled from typical mid-range 18 V drill/driver construction; masses and costs are engineering estimates, not measurements of a specific product.
Replace with your own teardown: photos of each layer, kitchen-scale masses, and calipers on the gears.

fmea.cause: Repeated stalls at max clutch setting heat the plastic
fmea.action: PA66-GF or sintered stage-1 planets on the high-torque SKU; thermal derating in firmware

fmea.cause: Commutator wear over about 60 h duty
fmea.action: Brushless upgrade path; or brush access door

fmea.cause: Inrush at stall with a fresh battery
fmea.action: MOSFET switching with the mechanical contact only as a signal

fmea.cause: Spring stressed near yield at max setting
fmea.action: Re-check spring index and max shear stress; shot peen

fmea.cause: Thin boss wall at screw F03-1
fmea.action: Add gussets; core out to uniform 2.2 mm wall

design_signals.title: Clamshell with lay-in architecture
design_signals.evidence: Every internal module drops into the left half; the right half closes it all with 9 screws.
design_signals.why: Assembly is top-down in one fixture with no flipping. The cost is that every repair starts by opening the whole tool.

design_signals.title: Mixed-material gear train
design_signals.evidence: Plastic ring gear and stage-1 planets, sintered steel stage 2.
design_signals.why: Plastic where speed is high and torque is low; steel where torque is high. Noise drops too.

design_signals.title: Clutch built into the ring gear
design_signals.evidence: The stage-2 ring gear face carries the ball ramps; the collar only loads the spring.
design_signals.why: No separate clutch housing, so fewer parts and a shorter nose.

design_signals.title: Shift by locking the carrier
design_signals.evidence: The shift ring slides to lock stage 2 to the housing (low) or to the carrier (high).
design_signals.why: Two speeds from one extra part instead of a second gear set.

opportunities.title: Plug the motor in
opportunities.change: Replace the 4 solder joints with a keyed 2-pin connector on the motor end cap
opportunities.impact: Cuts about 30 s of assembly, makes the motor a 2-minute swap

opportunities.title: Mold the thrust washers away
opportunities.change: Add a bearing shoulder on the stage-1 carrier and a molded thrust face on the ring gear
opportunities.impact: Removes 3 small parts that fall out during service

opportunities.title: Fewer, standard clamshell screws plus front snap hooks
opportunities.change: Two snap hooks at the nose, 6 screws in place of 9, standard T10
opportunities.impact: Faster close-up, opens with a normal driver

opportunities.title: Brushless motor and MOSFET switching
opportunities.change: Brushless motor with the PWM board; the trigger becomes a sensor
opportunities.impact: Removes the top two wear modes and the welded-contact hazard

verdict: A well-optimized clamshell: the gearbox and integrated clutch are lean, and plastic is used where it is safe. Assembly is dominated by the harness and the solder joints rather than by the mechanics, and repairability is held back by security screws and by soldered motor leads. Switching to plug-in motor leads and standard screws costs nothing and makes the motor and switch user-replaceable. Brushless is the real next product, not a cost-down.
